outline.description: Sets out the factual background, charges, trial events, verdict, sentence, and issues raised on appeal to frame the court’s analysis.
subtopics: November 19–20, 2020 incident: confinement of D.F. at gunpoint, threats, assault, flight, and standoff with police
Recovery of D.F.’s phone, knife, and sawed-off Marlin .22 rifle; DNA match to Cutbank; eyewitness identifications of the rifle
Charges: felon-in-possession under 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(g)(1), 924(e) (ACCA)
Jury verdicts: possession and at least three prior violent felonies (triggering ACCA)
Sentence: total offense level 35, CHC VI, Guidelines range 292–365 months; 292-month sentence imposed
Issues on appeal: multiple evidentiary/procedural rulings and application of USSG § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B)

outline.description: Explains why testimony about prior sightings of the same sawed-off rifle was admissible as intrinsic evidence relevant to proving possession, rather than impermissible propensity evidence.
subtopics: Defense motion in limine to exclude D.F. and C.F. testimony about prior sightings of the rifle
District court’s ruling: evidence is intrinsic and probative of continuous possession and control
Eighth Circuit authority: United States v. Battle—prior possession of the same weapon is directly relevant to later possession
Trial testimony: D.F. saw rifle a “handful of times”; C.F. saw it “once or twice” before
Standard of review: abuse of discretion; affirmance of admission as intrinsic evidence

outline.description: Analyzes challenges concerning out-of-court statements, the timing and necessity of limiting instructions, and Confrontation Clause compliance.
subtopics: Defense request for preemptive jury instruction limiting use of D.F.’s statements to police
Government’s position: statements used for context of police response; bench instruction if needed
Legal standards: United States v. Bennett (discretion on timing/need for limiting instructions)
Record findings: no hearsay admitted; D.F. testified at trial
Confrontation Clause satisfied when declarant testifies: United States v. Charboneau
Holding: no abuse of discretion

outline.chapter_title: Cross-Examination Boundaries, Rule 403, Authentication, and Harmless Error
outline.description: Addresses evidentiary rulings arising during cross-examination, including a witness’s explanation for inconsistencies, limits on using police reports, and the court’s harmless-error analysis.
subtopics: D.F.’s explanation for inconsistent statements (discomfort with guns; sister killed by a gun)
Rule 403 assessment: no unfair prejudice or confusion; district court’s broad discretion (Sprint/United Mgmt. Co. v. Mendelsohn)
C.F. also referenced the sister’s death without objection
Impeachment via prior statements to police: court allowed questioning but barred reading from police report absent foundation
Authentication requirement for extrinsic impeachment evidence: United States v. Cumbie
Appellee’s unnecessary expansion of issues; court’s observation but merits resolved regardless
Harmless error and cumulative error standards: United States v. DeMarce; United States v. Keys
Conclusion: any alleged errors did not substantially sway the verdict given strong testimonial and physical evidence

outline.chapter_title: Sentencing: § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) Enhancement, ACCA Interaction, and Reasonableness Review
outline.description: Explains the court’s approval of the four-level enhancement for using or possessing a firearm in connection with another felony, interaction with ACCA/Guidelines, and the within-Guidelines sentence’s reasonableness.
subtopics: PSR calculations: base level 26 (sawed-off firearm + prior crimes of violence), +3 (obliterated serial number), +2 (reckless endangerment during flight), +4 (§ 2K2.1(b)(6)(B) in connection with another felony) = offense level 35; CHC VI
Application Note 14(C): enhancement applies regardless of separate charge or conviction
District court adopted PSR facts without objection; no clear error under United States v. Dunn
Defense argument: enhancement yields a sentence greater than necessary under § 3553(a); comparison to ACCA guideline offense level 34 and rule that higher offense level applies (USSG § 4B1.4(b))
Procedural framework: correct Guidelines calculation required (Gall; Rosales-Mireles)
Substantive review: within-Guidelines sentences presumed reasonable (Goodhouse); court considered § 3553(a) and defense arguments (Masood; Maluoth)
Aggravating facts supporting sentence: extensive violent/firearm-related history; domestic abuse, confinement, assault; injury to officer during resistance
Holding: no procedural error; no abuse of discretion; sentence affirmed
